source: independent validator: research_education, validating another researcher's iDFAX story

claims.text: UTHealth Houston published its iDFAX account on September 16, 2026.
claims.statement: UTHealth Houston published its iDFAX account on September 16, 2026.

claims.text: UTHealth Houston reports iDFAX has moved into everyday clinical operations.
claims.statement: UTHealth Houston reports iDFAX has moved into everyday clinical operations.
claims.quote: That integration of research and clinical operations was critical to moving iDFAX beyond a promising AI concept and into everyday use, said Babatope Fatuyi, chief health innovation officer at UTHealth Houston.
claims.note: Attributed institutional account. This validator did not access a clinical production system.
claims.evidence_excerpt_scope: Full supporting source sentence or paragraph from independent web re-fetch; may include surrounding source metrics not adopted in narration.

claims.text: Before iDFAX, clinical staff manually reviewed medical faxes and entered data into the electronic health record system.
claims.statement: Before iDFAX, clinical staff manually reviewed medical faxes and entered data into the electronic health record system.
claims.quote: Before iDFax, UTHealth Houston’s legacy fax-based communication workflow consumed 82–150 seconds of staff time per fax. Healthcare staff manually reviewed, categorized, routed, and entered data into the Epic EHR system, creating costly bottlenecks that delayed patient care. With hundreds of thousands of medical faxes flowing through the system annually, this manual approach was unsustainable.
claims.source: AWS Public Sector Blog, coauthored by UTHealth and AWS participants
claims.note: UTHealth September report also describes manual review, identifying patient information and document entry; no inference that all present-day manual review has vanished.
claims.evidence_excerpt_scope: Full supporting source sentence or paragraph from independent web re-fetch; may include surrounding source metrics not adopted in narration.

claims.text: The technical account describes extraction of physician and patient data to connect fax content with patient records in Epic.
claims.statement: The technical account describes extraction of physician and patient data to connect fax content with patient records in Epic.
claims.quote: iDFax connects fax content to patient records through automatic extraction of physician and patient data for identity retrieval and record assignment with Epic.
claims.source: AWS Public Sector Blog, coauthored by UTHealth and AWS participants
claims.note: Simplifying Epic EHR record to chart in narration is faithful. Do not infer perfect matching or autonomous medical decision making.
claims.evidence_excerpt_scope: Full supporting source sentence or paragraph from independent web re-fetch; may include surrounding source metrics not adopted in narration.

claims.text: The technical account describes automated document categorization, splitting and de-duplication.
claims.statement: The technical account describes automated document categorization, splitting and de-duplication.
claims.quote: The solution automates key processes such as document categorization, splitting, and de-duplication, improving document organization quality while reducing processing errors.
claims.source: AWS Public Sector Blog, coauthored by UTHealth and AWS participants
claims.note: Sort and separate are faithful plain-language paraphrases. No invented fax content or actual patient data.

claims.text: UTHealth Houston reports staff time saved by iDFAX.
claims.statement: UTHealth Houston reports staff time saved by iDFAX.
claims.quote: Since its implementation, iDFAX has processed more than 1.8 million faxes, including more than 100,000 per month, and saved more than 73,000 hours of staff time.
claims.note: Institution-reported administrative time, not independently measured clinical outcome. The script deliberately drops all savings magnitudes.

claims.text: The September 16 university report supplies no appointment waiting-time measurement.
claims.statement: The September 16 university report supplies no appointment waiting-time measurement.
claims.value_text: No appointment waiting times in this report
claims.quote: Since its implementation, iDFAX has processed more than 1.8 million faxes, including more than 100,000 per month, and saved more than 73,000 hours of staff time.
claims.note: Verified source-scope audit from full page read. The quoted phrase identifies the reported metric; it does not directly state the absence. No sentence or table in this report measures time from referral to patient appointment. This claim must not become a claim that the institution never measures waits or that care is faster/slower.

claims.text: The July AWS technical account describes a launched Transcribe Order feature for referral processing.
claims.statement: The July AWS technical account describes a launched Transcribe Order feature for referral processing.
claims.quote: The success of iDFax provides a foundation for UTHealth Houston’s broader digital transformation strategy. The system’s proven capabilities in document processing and workflow automation create a platform for expanding AI initiatives across the organization, including the recently launched Transcribe Order feature, which enables faster referral processing with significantly reduced manual entry.
claims.source: AWS Public Sector Blog, coauthored by UTHealth and AWS participants
claims.note: July source perspective. Do not say launched today, not yet launched, or that clinic teams announced an ongoing study.

rejected.claim: The system/report does not measure how long patients wait for appointments.
rejected.reason: A published report omitting a measure cannot establish that the system or institution never measures it. Replaced with a statement bounded to the September report.

rejected.claim: Clinic teams are still refining the workflow, including referral orders.
rejected.reason: Sources establish technical evolution and a launched feature, but not this actor and present-day activity. Replaced with an explicit editorial question for clinic leaders.

rejected.claim: Reported savings prove earlier patient appointments or better clinical outcomes.
rejected.reason: Administrative processing/time figures and claimed impact are not a measured appointment-wait or patient outcome study. No care outcome is asserted.

rejected.claim: Every fax still requires manual human approval, or all human review was removed.
rejected.reason: Neither universal is stated. Sources describe partial workflow automation and record integration.

rejected.claim: iDFAX launched on September 16 or September 17, 2026.
rejected.reason: September 16 is the university report date; both sources describe earlier pilot and deployment.

rejected.claim: Large staff-hour, cost, percent, or appointment-equivalent savings as independently established benefits.
rejected.reason: Sources are institutional/vendor accounts with differently scoped figures. The film drops magnitudes and appointment equivalents; only attributed time-saved statement remains.

rejected.claim: The animated sample fax demonstrates measured system accuracy or is real patient information.
rejected.reason: No production system or patient record was inspected. Animation must remain a labelled illustration.
